The dress was longer than the doll and the sleeves were too wide. Lily was sad. She wanted her doll to look nice. She said to her doll, "I'm sorry, you can't wear this dress. It's too big for you. You know you are not supposed to touch them. They are not for you. They are for me. You could have ruined them. You have to be more careful."

Her mom sighed. She was not really mad at Lily. She knew Lily was just curious and liked to play. She said to Lily, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. But you have to remember to ask me before you use my things. And you have to put them back where they belong. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and houses and cars. Sara has a big tower with many colors. Ben has a small house with a door and a window.

"Look at my tower!" Sara says. "It is very high and pretty. How many inches do you think it is?"

Ben looks at Sara's tower. He wants to have a high tower too. He takes some blocks from his house and puts them on top of each other. His house becomes smaller and his tower becomes bigger.

"Stop!" Sara says. "Those are my blocks! You can't take them!"

Ben does not stop. He takes more blocks from Sara's tower and adds them to his own. Sara's tower becomes smaller and smaller. Ben's tower becomes bigger and bigger.

"Stop! Stop! Stop!" Sara says. She is angry and sad. She tries to grab her blocks back, but Ben pushes her away.

"Go away!" Ben says. "This is my tower now. It is the highest and best tower ever. I am very proud of it."

Sara starts to cry. She runs to Mom and tells her what Ben did. Mom comes to see the towers. She is not happy with Ben.

"Ben, that was not nice of you," Mom says. "You should not take Sara's blocks without asking. You should share and play nicely. How do you think Sara feels?"

Ben looks at Sara. She is still crying and holding Mom's hand. He feels sorry for her. He remembers that Sara is his sister and his friend.

"I feel bad," Ben says. "I am sorry, Sara. I should not have taken your blocks. Can we share and play together?"

Sara wipes her tears and smiles. She nods and hugs Ben.

"Thank you, Ben," Sara says. "I forgive you. I like your tower, but I like you more."

Mom smiles and hugs them both.

"I am proud of you, Sara and Ben," Mom says. "You are good siblings and good friends. Now, let's see if we can build something together with all the blocks."

"Ben, do you think the sun is alive?" Sara asks.

"I don't know, Sara. Maybe the sun is alive. Maybe it has a face and a voice and can talk to us," Ben says.

They try to talk to the sun. They say hello and ask how it is. But the sun does not answer. It just shines and shines.

"Ben, I think the sun is too far away to hear us. Or maybe it is too busy to talk to us," Sara says.

"Maybe, Sara. Or maybe the sun is too intelligent to talk to us. Maybe it knows things that we don't know," Ben says.

They stare at the sun some more. They think the sun is very smart and very beautiful. They wish they could be friends with the sun. They smile and wave at the sun. The sun smiles and waves back. At least, that is what they imagine.

"Where is it, Ben? Where is our treasure?" Anna cried.

"Wow, you are good at tying, Tom. Can you teach me how to do it?" Lily asked, holding the star in her hand.

"Sure, Lily. It is easy. You just make a loop and then pull the end through the loop. Like this," Tom said, taking the star and the string from Lily and demonstrating the steps.

Lily watched carefully and tried to copy Tom. She made a loop and pulled the end through the loop. But she pulled too hard and the string broke. The star fell to the floor and made a loud noise.

"Oh no, I broke it! Mom and dad will be mad at me!" Lily cried, feeling scared.

Lily sniffed and smiled a little. She hugged Tom back and said, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I love you too. And you are right. We have many more ornaments. Let's find another star for me."

Tom and Lily wiped their eyes and looked at the box. They saw a shiny blue star that was bigger and prettier than the yellow one. They both liked it and decided to use it. Tom tied a new string to the star and helped Lily hang it on the top of the tree. It looked beautiful.

"Mom, can you show me how to sew?" Lily said.

"Sure, honey. Sewing is fun, but you have to be careful with the needle. It is very sharp and can hurt you if you poke yourself," Mom said.

Mom showed Lily how to hold the needle and thread and how to make stitches on the cloth. Lily watched and listened carefully. Then she tried to do it by herself.

She put the needle through the cloth and pulled the thread. She did it again and again. She was making a seam. She felt proud of herself.

But then she made a mistake. She pulled the thread too hard and the needle slipped out of her hand. It fell on the floor and rolled under the bed.

"Oh no! Where is the needle?" Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily. We can find it. But first, let's put on some shoes. We don't want to step on the needle and hurt our feet," Mom said.

They put on their shoes and looked under the bed. They saw the needle shining in the dust. Mom reached for it and picked it up.

"Here it is, Lily. Be careful when you take it. Hold it by the eye, not by the point," Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. I will be more careful next time. I want to finish my dress for my doll. She will look so pretty," Lily said.

They went back to the table and continued sewing. Lily tried to make small and neat stitches. She was happy to learn something new. She loved her mom and her doll.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play outside in the snow. They have a big snowman and a red sled. They have fun every day.

One day, Lily and Ben hear a loud noise. They look up and see a big truck. The truck is coming to their street. The truck has a big shovel. The shovel is for moving the snow.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "The truck will take our snowman and our sled!"

Ben is scared. He runs to the house. He grabs his coat and goes inside. He does not want to lose his snowman and his sled.

Lily is brave. She runs to the snowman and the sled. She hugs them. She does not want to let them go.

"Please, please, don't take our snowman and our sled!" she says to the truck.

The truck driver sees Lily. He stops the truck. He gets out. He walks to Lily.

"Hello, little girl," he says. "Why are you hugging your snowman and your sled?"

Lily looks at him. She has tears in her eyes.

"Because they are ours," she says. "We made them. We love them. Please don't take them away!"

The truck driver smiles. He is kind. He understands.

"I see," he says. "Well, I have to clear the snow from the street. But I won't take your snowman and your sled. I will move them to your yard. Is that okay?"

Lily nods. She is happy. She says thank you.

The end.

Moral value: Be brave and face your problems.

One day, Lily and Ben went to the farm with their mom. They saw many animals, like cows, pigs, sheep and chickens. Lily liked the chickens best. She wanted to pet them and feed them.

"Can I fill this cup with corn and give it to the chickens, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey, but be careful. Don't go too close to the fence. The chickens might peck you," mom said.

Lily nodded and filled the cup with corn. She walked slowly to the fence and threw some corn to the chickens. The chickens clucked and ran to eat the corn. Lily smiled and threw more corn.

Ben saw what Lily was doing and wanted to join her. He filled his cup with corn too. But he was naughty. He did not listen to mom. He went too close to the fence and tried to touch a chicken.

"Hey, chicken, let me pet you," Ben said.

But the chicken did not like that. It pecked Ben's hand and made him cry.

"Ow, ow, ow! Mom, the chicken bit me!" Ben shouted.

Mom ran to Ben and hugged him. She checked his hand and saw a small scratch.

"Oh, Ben, I told you to be careful. The chicken was scared of you. You should not try to touch it. It might have germs too. Let me clean your hand and put a band-aid on it," mom said.

Lily came to Ben and said sorry.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I did not mean to make you cry. Do you want to share my corn with the chickens?" Lily asked.

Ben sniffed and nodded. He wiped his tears and smiled.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister. I will be nice to the chickens too," Ben said.

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Ben. I'm proud of you. And I'm proud of you too, Lily. You are both very sweet. Now, let's go and see the other animals, okay?"

Lily and Ben agreed and followed mom. They had fun at the farm and learned to be kind to the animals. They also learned to listen to mom and be careful. They did not want to be naughty again.

"But it looks so fun!" Ben said. He kicked the lock and it broke. He opened the gate and ran to the path.

"Ben, wait!" Anna said. She followed him, but she was scared.

They ran along the path until they came to a deep hole. Ben did not see it and fell in. He cried for help.

"Ben, are you okay?" Anna said. She looked down and saw him at the bottom of the hole. He was hurt and dirty.

"Anna, help me!" Ben said. He was sorry he did not listen to Anna.

He pulled him out of the hole and took him to his truck. He drove them back to their house and told their parents what happened.

Anna visited him every day and read him stories. She was glad he was okay, but she wished he had listened to her. She hoped he learned his lesson.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents and your sister. They know what's best for you. Don't go to places that are not safe. You might get hurt or lost.

Lily loved strawberries. She liked to eat them with her breakfast, with her lunch, and with her snack. She liked to pick them from the garden, wash them in the sink, and bite them with her teeth. She liked how they were red and sweet and juicy.

One day, Lily went to the store with her mom. She saw a big basket of strawberries on a shelf. She wanted to have some. She ran to the basket and grabbed a handful of strawberries. She put them in her mouth and chewed.

"Hey, stop that!" a voice said. Lily looked up and saw a man in a blue shirt. He worked at the store. He looked angry. "You can't eat the strawberries without paying. That's stealing. Give them back."

Lily did not want to give them back. She liked the strawberries. She wanted more. She spat out the seeds and said, "No! I want strawberries. Give me strawberries."

The man shook his head. He said, "No, you can't have strawberries. You have to pay for them. If you don't, I will call your mom."

Lily did not like the man. She did not like his voice. She did not like his shirt. She did not like his words. She felt uncomfortable. She started to cry. She said, "No, no, no! I demand strawberries. I demand strawberries."

The man sighed. He said, "You are a very naughty girl. You are making a mess. You are making a noise. You are making trouble. Where is your mom?"

Lily did not answer. She cried louder. She said, "I demand strawberries. I demand strawberries."

The man looked around. He saw Lily's mom. She was at the other end of the store. She was looking at some bread. She did not see Lily. She did not hear Lily. She did not know Lily was in trouble.

The man waved his hand. He said, "Hey, lady! Is this your kid? She is eating the strawberries without paying. She is demanding more. She is making a scene. Come and get her."

Lily's mom heard the man. She turned around. She saw Lily. She saw the strawberries. She saw the mess. She saw the people staring. She felt embarrassed. She ran to Lily. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? Why are you eating the strawberries? Why are you crying? Why are you demanding more? You are being very rude. You are being very bad. You have to say sorry. You have to pay. You have to stop."

Lily looked at her mom. She saw her face. She saw her eyes. She saw her mouth. She felt scared. She felt sorry. She felt sad. She stopped crying. She said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, man. I like strawberries. I want strawberries. But I was wrong. I was bad. I will pay. I will stop."

Lily's mom hugged Lily. She said, "It's okay, Lily. I love you. But you have to learn. You can't eat the strawberries without paying. You can't demand more. You have to ask nicely. You have to share. You have to be polite. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will be good. I will be nice. I will be polite."

Lily's mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Lily. I'm proud of you. Now, let's pay for the strawberries. And then, let's go home. And then, let's have some strawberries. But only a few. And only if you say please."

Lily smiled. She said, "Okay, mom. Thank you, mom. Please, mom. Can I have some strawberries?"

The end.

"Hello, gorilla!" Tom said. "Do you want to play with me? I have a ball. You can throw it and catch it. It is fun!"

But the gorilla did not say anything. He did not look at Tom. He looked at the sky.

Tom tried again. He made funny faces at the gorilla. He jumped up and down. He rolled the ball on the floor. He hoped the gorilla would laugh or join him. But the gorilla did not care. He yawned and scratched his head.

Tom thought about what Mom said. He looked at the gorilla again. He saw that the gorilla was not mean or rude. He was just quiet and calm. He did not need a ball or a friend. He had his rock and his sky.

Tom nodded and smiled. He said, "I understand, Mom. The gorilla is not stubborn. He is just gorilla. And I like him anyway."

He waved at the gorilla one last time. The gorilla did not wave back. But he did something else. He winked at Tom. Tom was surprised and happy. He felt like the gorilla was saying, "Thank you for being nice to me. Goodbye, little human."

Tom and Lily followed Mom to see the next animal. They had a good day at the zoo. And Tom never forgot the gorilla who winked at him.

Then, the little ball had an idea. It made itself very small and slipped out of the dog's mouth. The dog tried to catch the little ball again, but it was too clever. The little ball rolled away as fast as it could until it was safe and sound. From that day on, the little ball was more careful and always made sure to stay away from the mischievous dog.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He liked to play in his garden. One day, he saw a tree and wanted to climb it. He climbed and climbed until he reached the top. From there, he saw something strange in the garden. It was an unknown creature! Timmy got scared and fell from the tree. He hurt himself badly and had to go to the hospital. 

The doctors tried to help Timmy, but he was too hurt. He had to stay in the hospital for a long time. When he finally went home, he couldn't play in the garden anymore. He was sad because he loved his garden so much. Timmy learned that sometimes it's not safe to climb trees and explore unknown things.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, his mommy gave him a task to clean his room. Timmy didn't want to do it because it was a miserable task. He wanted to play with his toys instead.

But then, his mommy said, "Timmy, if you clean your room, we can go to the park and follow the ducks." Timmy loved the park and the ducks, so he decided to do the task.

After he finished cleaning, he went to his mommy and said, "Mommy, I did the task. Can we go to the park now and follow the ducks?" His mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Timmy. Let's go!" So, they went to the park and had a great time following the ducks together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie was very happy and loved to sing all day long. One day, Tweetie met a gray cat named Whiskers. Whiskers was troubled because he was very hungry and had not eaten anything for days. 

Whiskers asked Tweetie, "Can you help me find some food?" Tweetie replied, "Yes, I can help you find some food." So, they went on a journey to find some food. 

After a while, they found a big field of seeds. Tweetie said, "Look, Whiskers! We have found some food!" Whiskers was very happy and ate all the seeds. But then, Whiskers ate Tweetie too! 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat oatmeal for breakfast. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. They saw a boy named Timmy who was eating a cookie. Lily asked Timmy if she could have a bite of his cookie, but he said no and teased her by sticking his tongue out.

Lily felt sad and went to sit under a tree. Her friend, Sarah, saw that Lily was upset and asked her what was wrong. Lily told Sarah about Timmy teasing her and not sharing his cookie. Sarah was very kind and offered to share her oatmeal with Lily. Lily felt much better and thanked Sarah for being such a good friend.

The next day, Lily brought some oatmeal to share with her friends at the park. When Timmy saw how kind Lily was being by sharing her oatmeal, he felt bad for teasing her and not sharing his cookie. He apologized to Lily and they all enjoyed eating oatmeal together. From then on, Timmy learned that being kind was much better than teasing others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her family. One day, Lily went to the attic to play with her toys. She saw a cobweb on the floor and said, "Ew, that's filthy!"

Suddenly, she heard a noise and turned around. She saw her little brother, Timmy, coming up the stairs. Timmy said, "Lily, can I play with you?" Lily said, "Sure, but be careful not to break anything."

They played together for a while, but then Timmy accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke into many pieces. Lily said, "Oh no, Mommy will be so upset. We have to clean it up before she sees." They cleaned up the mess and made sure to be more careful next time.

Once upon a time, there was a man named John. John loved to drive his car. One day, while he was driving, he saw a deer on the road. The deer looked anxious and scared.

John stopped his car and got out. He said to the deer, "Don't be afraid, little deer. I won't hurt you. I'll drive slowly and let you cross the road safely."

The deer looked at John and said, "Thank you, kind man. You are so nice to me." John smiled and drove slowly, making sure the deer was safe. From that day on, John always drove carefully and looked out for animals on the road.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to clap her hands. She clapped when she was happy, and she clapped when she was sad. One day, Lily's mommy took her for a ride in their automobile. It was a normal day, but Lily was very excited to go for a ride.

As they were driving, Lily saw a big truck coming towards them. She pointed and said, "Look mommy, a big truck!" Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's a very big truck." But then, something unexpected happened. The big truck started to swerve and it looked like it was going to crash into their automobile.

Lily's mommy quickly turned the automobile to the side and they narrowly avoided the crash. Lily was scared and started to cry, but her mommy hugged her and said, "It's okay, we're safe now." From that day on, whenever they went for a ride, Lily always made sure to clap her hands extra loud to show how grateful she was to be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on a picnic with her family. Her mom had packed sandwiches with tuna for everyone to eat.

As they were eating, it started to rain. Lily's little brother, Timmy, started to cry because he didn't want to get wet. Lily saw that Timmy was sad and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. I will provide you with my umbrella."

You always think of others and provide for them, even when it means giving up something you want. That's a very special quality to have."

Lily felt proud of herself and realized that it's important to be kind and help others, even if it means getting a little wet in the process.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very sleepy and wanted to go to bed. Her mommy gave her a glass of milk to drink before she went to sleep. 

Lily drank the milk and felt very happy. She went to bed and closed her eyes. Suddenly, she heard a noise. She opened her eyes and saw a spider on the wall. She was very scared and didn't know what to do. 

She called out to her mommy, "Mommy, please answer me!" But her mommy was already asleep and didn't hear her. Lily tried to get out of bed to get away from the spider, but she accidentally knocked over the glass of milk. The glass broke and Lily got hurt. 

She cried and cried, but no one came to help her. She was all alone and very sad. From that day on, Lily never wanted to drink milk again.

Tim and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. They saw a big green plant with many sharp points. It was a cactus.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"It is a cactus. It is very prickly. Do not touch it," Tim said.

But Lily was curious. She wanted to see how the cactus felt. She reached out her hand and touched one of the points. Ouch! It hurt a lot. She cried and ran to Tim.

"Look, Tim, I have a boo-boo. The cactus poked me," Lily said, showing her finger.

Tim felt sorry for Lily. He wanted to help her. He saw a bucket of water near the hose. He had an idea.

"Come, Lily, I know what to do. We can soak your finger in the water. It will make it feel better," Tim said.

He took Lily's hand and led her to the bucket. He dipped her finger in the water. But the water was not clean. It was colorful. It had paint in it. Tim and Lily did not know that their dad had used the bucket to wash his brushes. The paint soaked Lily's finger and made it red and blue and yellow.

Lily looked at her finger and screamed. She did not like the colors. She wanted her finger to be normal. She was scared and angry. She pulled her hand out of the bucket and splashed water and paint all over Tim.

Tim was shocked and sad. He did not like the colors either. He wanted to be clean. He was wet and cold and sticky. He cried and ran to the house.

Their mom heard them and came out. She saw them and gasped. She was not happy. She was very mad. She scolded them and took them to the bathroom. She washed them and put a band-aid on Lily's finger. She told them to stay in their room and think about what they did. She said they were naughty and careless.

Tim and Lily felt bad. They did not mean to make a mess. They did not have fun. They had a bad day. They wished they had never seen the cactus.

Lila and Max were playing in the garden. They saw a big peach tree with many ripe peaches. They wanted to pick some and eat them.

"Let's get a peach, Max!" Lila said.

"OK, Lila. But how can we reach them? They are too high." Max said.

Lila had an idea. She saw a big rock near the tree. She said, "We can balance on the rock and grab a peach. I will go first. You hold my hand."

Lila climbed on the rock and stretched her arm. She touched a peach, but it was too far. She tried to lean more, but she lost her balance and fell off the rock.

"Ouch!" Lila cried. "That hurt!"

Max ran to her and hugged her. He said, "Are you OK, Lila? I'm sorry. You are very brave."

Lila smiled and said, "I'm OK, Max. Thank you. You are very kind."

They heard a voice from the house. It was their mom. She said, "Lila, Max, come inside. I have a surprise for you."

They ran to the house and saw a big bowl of peaches on the table. Their mom said, "I picked some peaches from the tree for you. They are sweet and juicy. You can have as many as you want."

Lila and Max were very happy. They said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

They ate the peaches and enjoyed them. They thought they were the most adorable peaches in the world.

Anna and Ben were twins who shared a room and a big wardrobe. They liked to play with their toys and dress up in different clothes. But sometimes they fought over who got to use the wardrobe first, or who had more space, or who made more mess. Then they would yell and cry and make a lot of noise.

One day, their mom had an idea. She said, "Why don't we separate the wardrobe into two parts? Then you can each have your own side and choose your own clothes. And you can keep your toys in your own baskets. That way, you won't fight so much and you'll be happier."

Anna and Ben liked the idea. They helped their mom move the wardrobe to the middle of the room and put a curtain in between. They sorted their clothes and toys and put them on their own sides. They decorated their sides with stickers and drawings. They were proud of their new spaces.

Now, Anna and Ben could play and dress up without bothering each other. They still shared some things, like books and games, and they still played together sometimes. But they also learned to respect each other's space and privacy. And they didn't make so much noise anymore. Their mom was happy, too. She said, "You see, sometimes separating can be a good thing. It can help you get along better and have more fun."

"Wow, so pretty!" Mia says, clapping her hands.

"Can we, Mom?" Ben asks.

"Sure, but be gentle and quiet," Mom says. "And stay alert. The bird might fly away if it gets scared."

Ben and Mia take some seeds and hold them in their palms. They walk slowly to the bird. The bird hops closer and pecks at the seeds.

"Thank you, bird!" Ben and Mia say softly.

The bird chirps and flaps its wings. It flies to another branch and sings.

"Thank you, Ben and Mia!" Mom says. "You are very kind and brave."

Ben and Mia smile and hug Mom. They are happy to share with the bird. They love the park and today.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with dolls and cars. But sometimes they fight over toys. Mommy tells them to behave and share. She says, "Be nice to each other. You are brother and sister."

Lily likes a pink dress and a purple hat. She says, "I am a princess. This is my style." Ben likes a blue shirt and a red cap. He says, "I am a firefighter. This is my style." They show each other their styles and say, "You look good."

But then Lily sees a shiny necklace in the box. She wants to wear it. She says, "This is mine. It is for princesses." Ben says, "No, it is not. It is for everyone. Let me see it." They start to pull and tug on the necklace. They get angry and yell at each other.

Mommy hears them and comes to the garage. She sees them fighting over the necklace. She says, "Stop it. What are you doing? This is not how you behave. You need to be honest and fair. The necklace is not yours. It is grandma's. She gave it to me. You can look at it, but you have to be careful and gentle. And you have to take turns."

Lily liked to help her mom with the mail. Every day, she would run to the mailbox and bring the letters and packages inside. She liked to look at the stamps and the pictures on the envelopes. Sometimes, she would open the mail for her mom and see what was inside.

One day, Lily saw a big package in the mailbox. It was wrapped in brown paper and had a lot of tape on it. Lily was very curious. She pulled the package out of the mailbox and ran inside. She put the package on the table and looked for scissors. She found a pair in the drawer and started to cut the tape.

She opened the package and saw a lot of paper and bubble wrap. She pushed them aside and saw something hairy. It was a big, furry hat. Lily thought it was funny. She put the hat on her head and looked in the mirror. She laughed at how silly she looked. She decided to show her mom.

She ran to the living room, where her mom was talking on the phone. She shouted, "Mom, look at me! I have a hairy hat!" She jumped in front of her mom and smiled.

Her mom gasped and dropped the phone. She looked at Lily and then at the package. She saw a note on the package. It said, "To Mom, from Aunt Sue. Happy birthday! I hope you like this hat. It's made from real alpaca wool. It's very warm and cozy. Love, Sue."

Her mom turned red and said, "Lily, you opened my birthday present! That was very rude. You should not open other people's mail. And you should not wear other people's hats. You embarrassed me in front of Aunt Sue. She heard you on the phone. How do you think she feels?"

Lily felt bad. She did not mean to be rude. She did not know it was her mom's birthday. She did not know what alpaca wool was. She just wanted to have fun. She took off the hat and said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I won't do it again. Can I say sorry to Aunt Sue?"

Her mom sighed and said, "Yes, you can. But first, you have to help me clean up this mess. And then, you have to give me a hug and a kiss. And then, you have to say happy birthday to me."

Lily nodded and said, "OK, Mom. I love you. Happy birthday." She hugged her mom and kissed her cheek. She hoped her mom was not too mad at her. She hoped Aunt Sue would forgive her. She hoped she would not open any more mail without asking. She learned her lesson.

"Can I see your car?" Lily asks Ben.

"OK, but be careful. It is very fast and loud," Ben says. He offers his car to Lily.

Lily takes the car and presses a button. The car makes a vroom sound and moves on the floor. She likes the car. It is fun and exciting.

"Hello, children. What are you playing with?" she asks.

Lily and Ben do not like Mrs. Jones. She is too nosy. They do not want to talk to her.

"Nothing," they say together.

They hide their toys behind their backs. They hope she will go away.

But Mrs. Jones does not go away. She steps into the living room and tries to see their toys.

"Oh, come on. Don't be shy. Let me see what you have. Is that a doll and a car? How nice. Can I play with them?" she asks.

Lily and Ben shake their heads. They do not want to share their toys with Mrs. Jones. They do not like her.

"Well, fine. Be that way. But you should learn to be more polite and friendly. Sharing is caring, you know," she says.

One day, a little pig went to the forest to look for food. He saw many fruits and nuts on the trees and on the ground. He was very happy and started to eat them. He did not see a big wolf hiding behind a bush. The wolf was hungry and wanted to eat the pig.

The wolf jumped out of the bush and said, "Hello, little pig. You look very tasty. I want to eat you for my lunch."

The pig was very scared and ran away. He saw a big rock and hid behind it. He hoped the wolf would not find him.

The wolf followed the pig and saw the rock. He said, "Little pig, little pig, come out of the rock. I know you are there. Don't be afraid. I just want to talk to you."

The pig did not believe the wolf. He said, "No, no, no. You are a bad wolf. You want to eat me. Go away. Leave me alone."

The wolf said, "Little pig, little pig, don't be rude. I have a gift for you. Look, I have a beautiful flower. It smells very nice. Come out and take it. I will not hurt you."

The pig was curious and liked flowers. He thought maybe the wolf was not so bad. He said, "A flower? Really? Let me see it."

The pig came out of the rock and saw the flower. It was red and yellow and had many petals. It looked very pretty. The pig reached out to take it.

But the wolf was lying. He grabbed the pig and said, "Ha, ha, ha. I got you, little pig. You are so foolish. You should not trust a wolf. Now you are my lunch."

The pig was very sad and cried. He said, "Please, please, please. Don't eat me, Mr. Wolf. I have a family and friends. They love me and need me. Please let me go."

The wolf said, "No, no, no. You are too delicious to let go. I will eat you now."

But then, the pig heard a loud noise. It was his father and his brothers. They came to the forest to look for him. They saw the wolf and the pig. They were very angry and brave. They said, "Let go of our brother, you evil wolf. Or we will make you sorry."

The wolf was scared and let go of the pig. He ran away as fast as he could. He did not want to fight with the other pigs.

The pig was very happy and hugged his father and his brothers. They said, "We are so glad you are safe, little pig. We were worried about you. Why did you go to the forest alone? Why did you trust the wolf? He is a liar and a killer. He is not your friend. He is your enemy."

The pig said, "I am sorry, father and brothers. I was hungry and greedy. I wanted to eat the fruits and nuts. I did not listen to you. I did not know the wolf was so bad. He tricked me with a flower. He almost ate me. I was very stupid."

His father and his brothers said, "It's okay, little pig. We forgive you. We love you. But you must learn from your mistake. You must not go to the forest alone. You must not talk to strangers. You must not believe everything you hear. You must be careful and smart. You must listen to us. We know what is best for you."

The pig said, "Yes, father and brothers. You are right. I will listen to you. I will be careful and smart. I will not go to the forest alone. I will not talk to strangers. I will not believe everything I hear. Thank you for saving me. You are the best family ever."

They all clapped and cheered. They went back to their home. They ate some corn and carrots. They sang some songs. They were very happy. They lived happily ever after.

The end.

Moral: Don't be greedy and foolish. Listen to your family and friends. Don't trust strangers. Be careful and smart.

One day, Lily went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. She whistled at them, but they did not whistle back. She was sad.

Then she saw a big bird with a long neck and legs. It was an ostrich. Lily thought it was funny. She whistled at it, hoping it would whistle back. But the ostrich did not whistle. It opened its mouth and made a loud noise. It sounded like a honk.

Lily was scared. She ran to her mom and dad and hugged them. "What was that?" she asked.

"That was the ostrich. It does not whistle, it honks," her dad explained.

"Why does it honk?" Lily wondered.

"Because that is how it talks to other ostriches. Every animal has its own way of making sounds," her mom said.

Lily was curious. She wanted to learn more about the animals and their sounds. She asked her mom and dad to take her to see more animals. She still liked to whistle, but she also wanted to listen. She was happy.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. But today, the park was very gray and cold. There was a lot of fog in the air, and they could not see very far.

"Mom, why is there so much fog?" Lily asked.

"Fog is when the air is full of tiny drops of water. Sometimes, when it is cold, the water does not fall as rain, but stays in the air. It makes everything look blurry and misty," mom explained.

"Can we still play in the park?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but be careful and stay close to me. The fog can make it hard to see and hear other people and things," mom said.

Ben and Lily nodded and ran to the swings. They pushed each other higher and higher, and laughed as they felt the wind on their faces. They did not notice that the fog was getting thicker and thicker. It was increasing, and soon they could not see the slide or the seesaw anymore.

"Mom, where are you?" Lily called out.

"I'm here, sweetie. Come back to me, please. The fog is too much now. We need to go home," mom said.

Ben and Lily stopped swinging and looked around. They could not see their mom, or the park gate, or the road. They felt scared and weak. They held hands and walked slowly towards the sound of mom's voice.

"Mom, we can't see you!" Ben shouted.

"I can't see you either, but I can hear you. Keep talking to me, and follow my voice. I'm right here, don't worry," mom said.

Ben and Lily kept talking and walking, until they finally saw mom's shape in the fog. They ran to her and hugged her tightly.

"Mom, we're sorry. We didn't mean to get lost," Lily said.

"It's okay, my loves. I'm sorry too. I didn't think the fog would increase so fast. Let's go home and have some hot chocolate, okay?" mom said.

They nodded and smiled. They were happy to be with mom, and to leave the fog behind. They learned that fog can be fun, but also dangerous. They decided to always listen to mom, and to stay close to her when they play in the park.

The big lamp showed the little lamp how to shine its light brighter and brighter. The little lamp practiced and practiced until it could shine its light so bright that the shadow disappeared! The room was bright and happy again.

"Let's go back to the tunnel," Lily said.

But the dog was faster than them and ran towards them. They tried to run away, but the dog caught up with them and bit Tom's leg. Tom cried out in pain and fell to the ground. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do.

"I am a fairy. I live in this forest. I saw you running after your dog, and I followed you. I want to help you find your way back to your mom," the fairy said.

"Can you do that? Can you find Spot and Mommy?" Ben asked, hopeful.

They said, "Bye, Lily. We will never forget you."

Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, you can almost reach it. But let's not get too close to the flame. It's hot!" Lily nodded and they watched the balloon float away in the sky. From that day on, Lily wasn't scared of scary things anymore because she knew her mommy would always be there to help her.

Once upon a time, there was a goat named Billy. Billy lived on a farm with his friends, the cows and the chickens. One day, Billy saw a modern barn with shiny windows. He wanted to go inside and explore, but the door was locked. 

Billy tried to push the door open, but it wouldn't budge. He needed to unlock it. He looked around and saw a key hanging on a hook. Billy jumped up and grabbed the key with his mouth. He put the key in the lock and turned it. The door clicked and opened. 

Billy was so excited to see the inside of the modern barn. He went in and saw a lot of new things like tractors and tools. He even saw some hay that was as soft as a pillow. Billy was happy he unlocked the door and got to explore the modern barn. From that day on, he visited the barn every chance he got.

"Wow, look at this!" Anna said. "It's a big puzzle with brilliant colors. It has animals and trees and flowers. Let's make it!"

"Yes, let's!" Ben said. They took the puzzle pieces out of the package and spread them on the floor. They started to look for the edges and corners.

But soon, they began to argue. Anna wanted to make the sky part first, but Ben wanted to make the grass part first. They pulled and pushed the pieces, trying to get their way.

"Stop it, Ben!" Anna said. "You're messing up the puzzle!"

"No, you stop it, Anna!" Ben said. "You're taking all the good pieces!"

They got louder and louder, until their mom came in. She saw the puzzle pieces all over the floor and the twins fighting.

"What's going on here?" she asked. "Why are you not sharing?"

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They felt ashamed. They knew they were being selfish and rude.

"We're sorry, mom," they said. "We both wanted to make the puzzle, but we couldn't agree on how to do it."

Mom smiled and hugged them. "I'm glad you're sorry, but you need to learn to cooperate. The puzzle is for both of you, and you can make it better if you work together. Why don't you take turns choosing the pieces, and help each other find the right spots?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They apologized to each other and decided to follow mom's advice. They took turns picking the pieces and praised each other's efforts. They had fun making the puzzle, and soon they finished it. It looked beautiful and bright.

They showed mom their puzzle and she was proud of them. "You did a great job, Anna and Ben!" she said. "You see, when you share and cooperate, you can make something wonderful. And you can also make each other happy."

Anna and Ben smiled and hugged mom. They learned their lesson and promised to be more kind and respectful to each other. They enjoyed their puzzle and their package, but they enjoyed their friendship more.

But the bus did not stop. It kept going and going. Lily felt worse and worse. She tried to tell her parents she was not well, but they did not hear her. They were busy looking at their phones and talking to each other.

Lily suffered a lot on the bus. She felt hot and cold. She felt pain in her tummy and her head. She felt like throwing up. She wanted to go home. She wanted her dolls and books. She wanted to be alone.

But she could not go home. She could not have her dolls and books. She could not be alone. She was stuck on the bus with her parents and many strangers. She was unhappy and miserable. She wished she never went on the holiday. She wished she never listened to her parents. She wished she was a different girl.

Tom and Mia were playing in the old barn. They liked to explore the dusty corners and find old things. But they had to be careful of the cobwebs. Some of them were very big and sticky, and had scary spiders in them.

"Look, Tom, I found a lantern!" Mia said, holding up a metal thing with a glass window. "Maybe we can make some light with it."

Tom was curious. He took the lantern from Mia and opened the window. Inside, he saw a wick and some oil. He remembered that his dad used matches to light candles at home. He wondered if he could do the same with the lantern.

He found a box of matches on a shelf. He took one out and struck it on the side of the box. It made a bright flame. He felt proud and excited. He brought the match close to the wick and lit it. The lantern glowed with a warm light.

"Wow, Tom, you did it!" Mia said, clapping her hands. "Now we can see better in the barn."

Tom smiled and lifted the lantern up. He wanted to show Mia the other things he could see. But he was not careful enough. He bumped the lantern against a beam. The glass window broke and the oil spilled out. The oil caught fire and spread to the wood and the hay. The barn was burning.

"Tom, Mia, get out of there!" They heard their dad's voice from outside. He had seen the smoke and ran to the barn. He grabbed Tom and Mia and pulled them out of the door. He hugged them and checked if they were hurt. They were not, but they were very scared and sorry.

"Dad, we're sorry, we didn't mean to burn the barn," Tom said, sobbing.

"I know, son, I know. It was an accident. But you have to be more careful with fire. It can be very dangerous. You could have been hurt, or worse," their dad said, sternly but gently.

He looked at the barn. It was too late to save it. The fire had eaten up most of it. He felt sad and angry, but also grateful. Grateful that his children were safe. Grateful that the fire had not reached the house or the animals. Grateful that he had seen the smoke in time.

He hugged Tom and Mia again. "I'm glad you're okay. I love you both. But you have to promise me that you will never play with fire again. Do you understand?"

Tom and Mia nodded. They understood. They felt ashamed and sorry. They also felt grateful. Grateful that their dad loved them. Grateful that he had saved them. Grateful that they still had each other.

But the monster did not go away. It moved closer to Lila's bed. Lila felt its breath on her face. She was very scared. She peeked from under the blanket and saw the monster's eye. It was yellow and bright. It looked at Lila and said, "Hello, little girl. Do you want to play with me?"

Lila was too scared to talk. She shook her head and said, "No, no, no. Go away, monster. You are bad. You are scary. I don't like you."

The monster smiled and said, "But I am not bad. I am not scary. I am your friend. I like you. I come to play with you every night. I appear when the light goes away. I am the dark."

Lila did not believe the monster. She did not want to be friends with the dark. She wanted the light. She wanted Mom and Dad. She cried and said, "No, no, no. You are not my friend. You are the dark. I hate the dark. I want the light. I want Mom and Dad. Help, help, help!"

The monster was sad. It did not understand why Lila hated it. It only wanted to have fun with Lila. It said, "Please, don't cry, little girl. Don't hate me. I am lonely. I have no friends. The light is mean to me. It makes me go away. It makes me invisible. You are the only one who can see me. You are the only one who can play with me. Please, be my friend."

But Lila did not listen to the monster. She kept crying and calling for Mom and Dad. She did not care if the monster was lonely. She did not care if the light was mean to it. She only cared about herself. She was selfish.

Then, Mom and Dad heard Lila's cries. They ran to her room and turned on the light. They saw Lila under the blanket, sobbing. They hugged her and asked her what was wrong. Lila pointed to the wall and said, "There was a monster. It was the dark. It wanted to play with me. It was bad. It was scary. I hate it."

Mom and Dad looked at the wall. They saw nothing. They said, "There is no monster, Lila. There is no dark. It was just a shadow. It was just your imagination. You don't have to be afraid. We are here. We love you."

Lila looked at the wall. She saw nothing. She felt silly. She said, "Sorry, Mom and Dad. I was silly. I was afraid. I love you."

Mom and Dad smiled and said, "It's okay, Lila. We understand. Everyone is afraid sometimes. But you have to be brave. You have to face your fears. You have to learn to like the dark. The dark is not bad. The dark is not scary. The dark is just the dark."

Lila nodded and said, "Okay, Mom and Dad. I will try. I will be brave. I will face my fears. I will learn to like the dark. The dark is just the dark."

Mom and Dad kissed Lila and tucked her in. They turned off the light and said, "Good night, Lila. Sleep well. We are here. We love you."

Lila closed her eye and said, "Good night, Mom and Dad. Sleep well. I am here. I love you."

Then, she fell asleep. She did not hear the monster's voice. She did not see the monster's eye. She did not know the monster was still there. It was still on the wall. It was still looking at Lila. It was still sad. It said, "Good night, little girl. Sleep well. I am here. I love you."

But then, Sam came in. Sam was Ben's big brother. He wanted to play too, but he did not like dolls. He said dolls were for babies. He grabbed Lily's doll and threw it away. Lily was very sad and angry. She cried and ran to Mom.

Ben did not like what Sam did. He wanted to get the doll back for Lily. He took his toy soldiers and attacked Sam. He said, "Give back the doll or I will make you surrender!" Sam laughed and said, "You are too small to make me surrender. You are a silly king."

Ben and Sam fought with their toys. They made a lot of noise and mess. Mom heard them and came in. She was not happy. She said, "Stop fighting right now! You are both in trouble. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

She gave Lily her doll and a hug. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Sam was very mean to you. He should not take your toys. You can play with whatever you like." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best."

Mom wrote a note for Sam and Ben. She said, "You need to say sorry to Lily and to each other. You need to share your toys and play nicely. If you don't, you will have no dessert tonight. And the dessert is your favorite: apple pie." She put the note on their door and left.

Sam and Ben saw the note. They felt bad. They did not want to miss the apple pie. They did not want to make Lily and Mom sad. They decided to say sorry. They knocked on Lily's door and said, "Lily, we are sorry. We were very mean to you. Can we play with you again?" Lily opened the door and said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be nice and fair. And you have to like my doll." Sam and Ben nodded and said, "OK, we will. We like your doll. She is very pretty."

They all went back to the fort and played together. They had more fun. They made the doll the princess of the fort and the toy soldiers her guards. They pretended to have a big feast with apple pie. They did not fight anymore. They were happy.

Mom came in and saw them. She smiled and said, "I'm glad you are playing nicely. You are good kids. You can have some real apple pie now. But first, you have to clean up the mess." They all said, "Yes, Mom." They cleaned up the mess and then ate the apple pie. It was very sweet and yummy. They did not like sour things. They liked sweet things. And they liked each other. The end.

The bird looked at Ben and said, "I sing because I am grateful for what I have. I have food, water, shelter and friends. I do not need much to be happy. I also do not hurt others with my words or actions. I am kind and gentle. That is how I sing so well."

But Blue did not come back. He flew out of the window and into the sky. He was free, but he was scared. He did not know where to go. He did not see Sara or his cage or his seeds. He only saw big birds and big cars and big noises.

Lily nodded. She looked at a big book on her uncle's desk. It had many words and numbers.

"What is this?" Lily asked.

"This is a law book," her uncle said. "It has the rules that everyone has to follow. Lawyers have to know the rules and use them to help their clients."

Lily was curious. She opened the book and tried to read it, but she did not understand the words.

"Can you read this?" Lily asked her uncle.

"Yes, I can," her uncle said. "But it took me a long time to learn. You have to go to school for many years to be a lawyer."

Lily felt a little discouraged. She wanted to be a lawyer like her uncle, but she did not know the rules or the words.

"Can I be a lawyer when I grow up?" Lily asked.

"Of course you can," her uncle said. "You just have to believe in yourself and work hard. You are a smart and brave girl, and you can do anything you want."

"Look, Lily, a parade!" Ben says. "Let's march with them!"

"OK, Ben, that sounds fun!" Lily says. They run to the parade and join the line. They march and clap and sing. They feel happy and excited.

But not everyone likes the parade. A man sits on a bench. He is lazy and grumpy. He does not like the noise and the music. He wants to read his book. He sees Lily and Ben. He thinks they are silly and noisy.

"Hey, you two, stop marching!" the man shouts. "You are ruining my peace!"

Lily and Ben hear the man. They are scared and sad. They stop marching. They look at the man. He looks angry and mean.

"Sorry, sir, we just wanted to have fun," Lily says.

"Yeah, we like the parade," Ben says.

"Well, I don't!" the man says. "Go away and leave me alone!"

Lily and Ben feel bad. They want to make the man happy. They think of a joke. They whisper to each other. They smile and nod.

"OK, sir, we will go away," Lily says. "But first, can we tell you a joke?"

"A joke?" the man says. "What joke?"

Lily and Ben say the joke together. They say:

"Why did the chicken cross the road?"

The man rolls his eyes. He says:

"I don't know, why?"

Lily and Ben say:

"To march with the parade!"

They laugh and giggle. They think the joke is funny. They hope the man will laugh too.

But the man does not laugh. He frowns and snorts. He says:

"That's not a joke, that's nonsense!"

He shakes his head and goes back to his book. He ignores Lily and Ben.

Lily and Ben shrug and smile. They think the man is silly and grumpy. They do not care what he says. They run back to the parade. They march and clap and sing. They feel happy and excited. They have fun.

Tom and Lily were very excited to see the fireworks. They had never seen them before. They wore warm coats and hats and went with their mom and dad to the park. There were many people and lights and noises.

"Look, mom, look!" Tom shouted, pointing at the sky. "Fireworks! They are so pretty and bright!"

"Yes, they are, Tom. They are very interesting. Do you know how they work?" Mom asked.

"No, how?" Lily asked.

"Well, they are like big rockets that fly very high and then break into many colors. They make loud sounds too. But they are not toys. They can be very dangerous if you touch them or play with them. You have to be careful and stay away from them." Mom explained.

"OK, mom. We will be careful. We just want to watch them." Tom and Lily said.

They watched the fireworks for a long time. They saw red, blue, green, yellow, and purple fireworks. They saw fireworks that looked like stars, flowers, hearts, and smileys. They oohed and aahed and clapped their hands. They had a lot of fun.

But then, something bad happened. One of the fireworks did not fly high enough. It fell down and landed near a trash can. It started a small fire. The fire grew bigger and bigger. It made smoke and heat.

"Fire! Fire!" People shouted. They ran away from the fire. They were scared and worried.

"Mom, dad, what's happening?" Tom and Lily asked. They were scared too.

"Don't worry, kids. We have to move away from the fire. It's not safe here. Come on, follow us." Mom and dad said. They took Tom and Lily by the hand and walked quickly to a safe place.

Soon, the firemen came. They had big trucks and hoses and helmets. They sprayed water on the fire. They put out the fire. They checked if anyone was hurt. They were brave and helpful.

"Wow, the firemen are amazing!" Tom said.

"Yes, they are. They saved the day. They stopped the fire." Lily said.

"Are you OK, kids? Are you hurt?" Mom and dad asked.

"We are OK, mom, dad. We are not hurt. But we are sad. The fire ruined the fireworks. They were so interesting." Tom and Lily said.

"I know, kids. It was a bad accident. But we are lucky that no one was badly hurt. And we still have each other. That's what matters most." Mom and dad said. They hugged Tom and Lily.

"Can we see the fireworks again someday?" Tom and Lily asked.

"Of course, kids. Someday, we will see the fireworks again. And they will be even more interesting and beautiful. But for now, let's go home and have some hot chocolate. How does that sound?" Mom and dad asked.

"That sounds good, mom, dad. We love you." Tom and Lily said.

They smiled and went home. They had a big adventure. They learned a lot. They were happy.

She kisses Ben's knee and rubs it gently. Ben stops crying and smiles. He says, "Thank you, Mom, you are nice. My knee feels better now."

Ben nods and says, "Yes, Mom, I'm ready. Let's go."

He takes Mom's hand and Lila's hand and they go out of the door. They leave their blocks behind, but they know they can play with them again when they come back. One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. She brought her colors and papers with her. She saw a big plane in the air and pointed at it. "Look, mom, look, dad, a plane!" she said. "Can we go in a plane someday?"

"Maybe, Anna, maybe," her mom said. "But planes are very expensive and far away. We have to save money and plan ahead."

Anna nodded. She understood. She wanted to go in a plane, but she also wanted to be good and help her mom and dad. She decided to draw a plane for them. She took a blue paper and a red color. She drew a big plane with wings and windows and a tail. She was very proud of her drawing. She wanted to add something more to make it special.

She looked around the park and saw a charming boy playing with a ball. He had curly hair and a big smile. He looked friendly and fun. Anna thought he would like to see her drawing. She walked over to him and said, "Hi, I'm Anna. Do you like planes?"

The boy looked at her and nodded. "Hi, I'm Leo. I love planes. They are fast and loud and cool. Can I see your drawing?"

Anna showed him her drawing. He liked it very much. He said, "Wow, that's a great plane. You are very good at drawing. Can I add something to it?"

Anna smiled. She liked Leo. He was nice and polite. She said, "Sure, what do you want to add?"

Leo took a yellow color and drew a sun in the corner of the paper. He said, "There, now the plane has a sun to shine on it. It looks happier and warmer."

Anna agreed. She liked the sun. It made the plane look brighter and more beautiful. She said, "Thank you, Leo. You are very good at adding. Do you want to be my friend?"

Leo nodded. He said, "Yes, Anna. I want to be your friend. You are very good at sharing. Do you want to play with me?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, Leo. I want to play with you. You are very good at making me happy. Do you want to draw more planes with me?"

Leo nodded. He said, "Yes, Anna. I want to draw more planes with you. You are very good at making me dream. Do you want to fly in a plane with me someday?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, Leo. I want to fly in a plane with you someday. You are very good at making me hope. Do you want to hug me?"

Leo nodded. He said, "Yes, Anna. I want to hug you. You are very good at making me love. Do you want to hug me?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, Leo. I want to hug you. You are very good at making me love. Do you want to hug me?"

They hugged each other and smiled. They were happy and hopeful. They had a new friend and a new dream. They had a plane and a sun. They had love.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of friendship, sharing, kindness, and optimism. It shows that even if you can't have what you want right away, you can still enjoy what you have and make the best of it. It also shows that by being open and generous, you can meet new people and discover new possibilities.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story uses foreshadowing or setup and payoff by introducing the plane as Anna's favorite thing to draw and her wish to fly in one, and then having her meet Leo, who shares her passion and adds a sun to her drawing, symbolizing their bright future together. The story also uses repetition and rhyme to create a rhythm and a connection between the characters.

Lily was a thoughtful girl who liked to ask questions. She wanted to know how things worked and why they were the way they were. One day, she asked her mom, "Mom, how do we feel things?"

Her mom smiled and said, "We feel things with our senses, like our eyes, ears, nose, mouth and skin. They help us know what is around us and how it makes us feel."

Lily thought for a moment and then said, "But how do we feel with our mouth? We only use it to eat and talk, right?"

Her mom said, "No, we can also feel with our mouth. For example, when you eat something sweet, like a cookie, your mouth feels happy and yummy. When you eat something sour, like a lemon, your mouth feels puckered and sour. When you eat something hot, like soup, your mouth feels warm and cozy. When you eat something cold, like ice cream, your mouth feels cold and refreshing. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I think so. Can I try to feel different things with my mouth?"

Her mom said, "Sure, but be careful not to put anything dirty or dangerous in your mouth, okay?"

Lily said, "Okay, mom. Thank you for teaching me how to feel with my mouth. You are the best mom ever!"

Her mom hugged her and said, "You are very welcome, Lily. You are a very smart and thoughtful girl. I love you very much!"

As they played, the weather got colder and colder. It started to freeze. Lily forgot about her purse and went home with her friends. The purse was left outside in the cold and it froze too.

The next day, Lily remembered her purse and went to find it. But when she found it, it was frozen and very hard. She tried to open it, but it broke into pieces. Lily was very sad. Her reliable purse was gone forever.

Jack slowly nodded his head. He wanted to help the bird. He picked it up and carried it to his house. He brought it inside and gave it some food and water.

The bird ate and drank, and soon it felt better. Jack smiled, happy that he had been able to help the bird. He nodded his head again and said goodbye to the bird. Then he opened the window so the bird could fly away.

He took some pieces of paper and drew a big picture of the rock. On the paper, the cone wrote a big word that said 'rock'. Then, he grabbed some paints and bright colours and started painting the words on the picture.

After the painting was finished, the cone decided to show it to the rock. He took the painting and put it in front of the rock. The rock stared at the picture and smiled. He finally understood what the cone was trying to tell him.

The cone and the rock became best friends. Every day they spent time together, playing and singing songs. Even though the rock couldn't hear the words, he still enjoyed the music very much.

The cone and the rock were very happy and they lived happily ever after.

The lion was getting mad and he was roaring louder and louder. Finally he found the alarm. It was a tiny box and it was making a weak sound. He pushed it with his paw and the noise stopped.

The lion was happy now and he went back to sleep in the cave. Everything was peaceful again.
